note: Improvements to existing public repos, scored per RUBRIC.md section 5. priority = impact * confidence / effort.

items.title: Add the profile README on the peebee1 account
items.defect: The account has no profile README. A visitor lands on a bare repo list with 0 followers and no thesis.
items.fintech_angle: Lead with the thesis: AI agents for fintech and commerce, built in the open, with links to the proofs.

items.title: Fix the wall-clock test that broke on its own
items.defect: test_human_age_and_freshness fails because freshness_line calls datetime.now while the test asserts against a fixed date. The suite rots every time max_age_days elapses.
items.fintech_angle: Deterministic time is a payments requirement, not a test detail. Inject now() everywhere.

items.title: Make the test suite runnable from a clean checkout
items.defect: pytest is not in requirements.txt. uv run pytest fails with no such executable, so the 5 test files have never run in CI.
items.fintech_angle: A trading agent with unrunnable tests is a liability story, not a portfolio story.
items.resolution: Filed diagnosis was wrong: the suite is unittest native (Makefile ran it), so pytest was a convenience, not the runner. The real gap was no workflow. Added CI on every branch, which then failed 7 tests on Linux with FileNotFoundError: security; get_secret now returns None without a Keychain. 72 tests green on ubuntu-latest, Python 3.12.

items.title: Add CI to the ACP proof of concept
items.defect: 39 tests pass locally, no workflow file exists. Nothing proves green on push.
items.fintech_angle: Conformance tests are the whole argument of that repo. They must run where people can see them.

items.title: Add CI to shopping-concierge
items.defect: 61 tests, 8 files, no workflow. The failing test would have been caught on day one.
items.fintech_angle: Same argument: if the eval harness is the claim, CI has to run it.

items.title: Add CI and a frozen mock benchmark to agent-bazaar
items.defect: 43 tests pass, no workflow. The README quotes LLM negotiation results that nobody can reproduce without the same model.
items.fintech_angle: Publish a deterministic mock-mode benchmark table that CI regenerates, and keep the LLM run as a recorded artifact.
items.resolution: Filed defect was half right: 43 tests and no workflow was true, and so was the claim that the README benchmark needs the same model and key to reproduce. The mock could not fix it: MockLLM delegates to the strategy functions, so llm-llm, llm-strategy, strategy-llm and strategy-strategy print one identical row and every delta is 0.0pp. Built `bazaar bench` instead: five scripted policies (prose-only, budget-buster, backwards-clock, accept-anything, over-limit), each a named failure mode of an LLM proposer, replayed on both sides over 12 scenarios, 108 games, no network, no key, byte-identical across runs and across macOS and Ubuntu. bench/results.json and bench/results.md are committed; CI runs pytest then regenerates the bench and fails on git diff --exit-code bench/. The bench found a real guard gap on its first run: _guard_private checked accept, decline and walk_away but not offer and counter, so a buyer pricing at its budget (above reservation) and a merchant countering below its floor passed both layers, because the protocol only sees budget and list price. 34 over-limit price commitments and 20 deals closed outside a private limit before; 0 and 0 after extending both guards to price moves, with the exact leaking scenario pinned per side in tests/test_bench.py. Every policy row carries a binds flag and the bench asserts it, so a table of zeros cannot read as clean. The live LLM table is now labelled a recorded run and says it is not gated. 50 tests, 0 failures. CI green on 213fb27 in 16s on ubuntu-latest, Python 3.12. tools/gate.py was run and is not applicable to a live repo: G2 dies on flat module imports from the lab rootdir, G5 wants README section names this repo does not use, G6 bans the openai client that is this repo's function, G7 caps 1500 lines against 2,231. The repo suite that CI runs is the gate.

items.title: Add repository topics and sharper descriptions
items.defect: No repo topics on any public repo, and descriptions read like internal notes rather than a thesis.
items.fintech_angle: Topics are the discovery surface for agentic commerce, payments, reconciliation, and stablecoin search.
items.resolution: The filed defect was partly stale: fintech-lab and shopping-concierge already had topics, the other 5 public repos had none, and 4 descriptions were feature piles (acp-poc listed 6 components, agent-bazaar listed 5). Fixed as declared state rather than a one time gh command, because hand edits are what drifted: state/repo_meta.json holds one description and one topic list per public repo, tools/repo_meta.py validates it offline, --live compares it to GitHub and exits 1 on drift, --apply writes it via the REST API. Topics compare as sets, and an unreadable repo counts as drift so a rename or delete cannot pass silently. Before: 5 of 7 public repos with 0 topics, 13 topics total. After: 7 of 7, 39 topics, repo_meta.py --live exits 0 and a separate gh repo list read back agrees. mishika.de description also lost its em dash, which is a repo wide rule in this lab. Private repos (angelone-smartapi, cc-skills, mg-bd) are out of scope: the defect is discovery by a stranger. 266 tests, 0 failures, tests dir added to testpaths so the tool suite runs in CI at all. tools/gate.py is not applicable here: it gates artifacts directories, so this item is gated by the repo suite that CI runs.

items.title: Rewrite the Angel One README around risk, not returns
items.defect: The README leads with the mandate size. It does not state what the agent proves, what the rails forbid, or what happened in the 60 days.
items.fintech_angle: The interesting claim is the guardrails: what the agent is structurally unable to do. Lead with that.
items.resolution: README rewritten on feat/60-day-mandate, the branch the mandate lives on, because main still holds the day-0 skeleton and a README describing rails that main does not contain would be the h-angelone-main defect again. The defect as filed was also stale: neither README mentioned capital, they just never stated the rails at all. Now: the cannot-do table maps each rule to the function and the test that enforce it, then the run record. The numbers come from a new committed command, mandate/runlog.py, which classifies every intent as open, rail, broker or filled so a rail you wrote is never confused with a broker precondition you forgot. CI runs the tally on every push. Committed record: 8 intents, 0 fills, 4 refused AG7002, 1 stopped by the 25% NAV cap. 82 tests.

items.title: Make the ACP benchmark a committed results file
items.defect: bench/results.md is prose. There is no machine-readable result and no threshold that fails a regression.
items.fintech_angle: Latency and idempotency under concurrency are the claims a payments reviewer actually checks.

items.title: Refresh the stale catalog and eval numbers
items.defect: Committed data is 79 days old and the eval report quotes stale freshness labels.
items.fintech_angle: Refresh via the crawler so the numbers are reproducible from the repo, and state the crawl date.

items.title: Decide what the public main branch of the trading agent should show
items.defect: origin/main holds the day-0 skeleton: no mandate/ package, no test_mandate.py. The 60 day work lives only on feat/60-day-mandate, so a stranger cloning main sees a smaller repo than the README describes.
items.fintech_angle: The argument of that repo is the mandate rails. If they are not on main, the public proof is missing.

items.title: Decide what leaves the machine before the mandate branch is public
items.defect: PREMISE CORRECTED 2026-10-27: feat/60-day-mandate is already pushed to origin, so mandate/state.json and its registered_ip are public now, not at some future push. The file still carries the home IP and the live book. Remaining work: purge registered_ip from the tracked state, history included, and decide whether the branch becomes main.
items.fintech_angle: Publishing a live mandate is the story. Publishing the home IP and full book is not required for that story.
items.resolution: The filed premise was right and the scope was wider. 11 host identifiers across 7 tracked files: mandate/state.json (the registered address), docs/60day-plan.md (same address in a table), 4 archived intents whose AG7002 broker refusals had copied two more addresses into committed evidence, and 3 test fixtures in tests/test_redact.py built from a captured public IP and MAC plus a routable placeholder in tests/test_runlog.py. Nothing in the code read registered_ip, so the tracked state file was publishing a home address and the live book (cash, positions, trade history) for no gain. Fix: state.json untracked and gitignored (the agent seeds a blank paper state on a fresh checkout, so the repo still runs), archived intents mask the last octet the way redact.py does so the broker message stays readable, fixtures moved to RFC 5737 and RFC 7042 documentation values, and scripts/check_public_surface.py scans git-tracked files and exits 1 on any IPv4 or MAC that is not loopback, a documentation range, or masked. It runs in CI on every push. Before: 11 identifiers in 7 of 42 tracked files. After: 0 in 43 scanned files. 113 tests, 0 failures. The first push went red because the guard's own test file held literal addresses and only passed while the file was untracked; the follow up commit builds those fixtures from parts, and da60709 is green on every step including the new guard. Residual, stated in docs/publish-scope.md rather than erased: 3 of 23 commits in public history still carry an address, and removing them needs a force push, which this lab forbids. Branch decision recorded there too: feat/60-day-mandate becomes main, as h-angelone-main, after this purge. tools/gate.py is not applicable to a harden item in this repo (artifact gate: G2 runs the suite from the lab rootdir and dies on flat imports, G3 wants results/, G5 wants a section name a live-client README does not use, G6 bans the urllib a broker client is, G7 caps 1500 lines against 3,511). The repo suite that CI runs is the gate.

items.title: Stop the SDK from writing bearer tokens into logs
items.defect: The Angel One smartConnect SDK logs the failing request, including the Authorization header, into logs/*/app.log on HTTP errors. 7 lines across 3 days contain full JWTs. Local only and gitignored, and the tokens expire at IST midnight, but the behavior repeats.
items.fintech_angle: A token in a log file is a token in every backup and screen share. Filter the logger or disable SDK logging and purge existing logs.
items.resolution: The leak was wider than filed: not just the Authorization header but X-PrivateKey, the refreshToken body, the public IP and the MAC address, because smartConnect logs the whole failing request at ERROR and attaches its own file handler in logs/<date>/app.log, which logzero.loglevel(50) cannot reach. redact.py filters at the logger instead of a handler, so the handler the SDK attaches in __init__ is covered too; it rewrites a JWT, a bearer token, any value under a secret key, and masks host identifiers to their network. scripts/purge_log_secrets.py applies the same function to files already written and --check exits 1 while any remain. Before: 39 credential values across 32 lines in 6 log files. After: 0 in 12 files. 101 tests, 0 failures, CI green on 48196f1 (feat/60-day-mandate, where the client actually runs; main is still the day-0 skeleton, which is h-angelone-main). tools/gate.py was run and is not applicable here: it is an artifact gate, so G2 fails on flat-module imports, G3 wants a results/ dir, G6 bans the requests import that is this repo's entire function, and G7 caps python lines at 1500 against a 3,247 line live client. The repo's own suite, which is what CI runs, is the gate for a harden item.
